limitations: No native video input: timestamped extracted frames are the actual perceptual input, unlike native-video API benchmarking.
No audio perception/transcription available; audio unassessed for all clips; spoken_dialogue is fail-open true.
Contact sheets use 640x360 maximum thumbnails, with original-resolution individual frames and original video available for denser inspection.
Input MP4 container metadata (including embedded generation-workflow tags) was stripped; decoded video streams are identical to the source clips.
Sparse visual sampling may miss events between sampled frames, especially the long clip at 1 fps.
Fresh delegated prompts restricted source access, but the filesystem was not sandboxed per task and tool reads were not independently audited.

validator_amendments.by: benchmark operator (parent session), after all 482 predictions were complete
validator_amendments.change: accept optional fractional seconds (MM:SS or MM:SS.fff); 89 findings in 46 jobs used sub-second timestamps on the 4 fps frame grid; 9 further timestamps in SS:cc form on 10 s clips (e.g. 06:75 = 6.75 s) are recorded as warnings, not errors

evaluation_policy.fresh_context_delegation: App-owned independent delegated task per invocation (T3 delegate_task, Claude Opus 5.5, effort high); sibling outputs were not supplied in task prompts.

media_adaptations: Frame fallback: timestamped JPEG contact sheets viewed with the Read tool rather than native-video input.
Thirteen short clips sampled at 4 fps; clip-01 sampled at 1 fps plus detected shot-boundary frames. Identical sampling to the 261027 GPT-6 Astra blind run.
Audio unassessed; spoken_dialogue=true triggers the audio role on every clip.
Shared contact sheets have at most 640x360 pixels per frame; native-resolution JPEGs and the MP4 were available for optional denser inspection. Individual tool reads were not audited.
Input container metadata stripped (decoded streams identical).
